doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Calloway's private train car, dignity and punctuality
summary: Williams and Hinton describe Calloway's own Pullman and baggage car with a Lincoln, and his insistence on cleanliness and punctuality.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: The things that he did, his visions of how to deal with what was at the time. For instance, he was one of the first, if not the first of the black entrepreneurs who would hire a train, you know a car, for just his group. And so they wouldn’t have to deal with other people.

And nobody did say anything because it was his car. And we’d get to a town and he could park it on the siding and the fellas would stay on, they’d eat on, and what have you, and relieve themselves. And then it came time to leave and they’d hook it up and take in on to the next place.
But that was a great comfort and innovation in those days, you know.

He was amazing. He had a whole Pullman car for himself, and a baggage car. He had a baggage car big enough to have a Lincoln, a green Lincoln in there, and he had his chauffeur. And the dignity of this man, he insisted on cleanliness, he insisted on punctuality. And nobody you can, if anybody was ever in Cab Calloway’s band would not come late on your gig. Because he’d say, “I’ve got to be here, you better be here.”
